title: Chapter 3 Quiz 13
description: Splitting a program into smaller parts and calling them.
instructions: Take your time: read each question carefully, then check your answer.

questions.question: What is a **subprogram**?
options: A named part of a program that is run when another part calls it
questions.explanation: A subprogram has a name, variables, instructions, a beginning and an end, but cannot run independently.

questions.question: Which instruction asks for the execution of a subprogram?
questions.explanation: The main program (or another subprogram) uses CALL.

questions.question: Which are advantages of subprograms?
questions.explanation: The course lists reusability, modularity and clarity.

questions.question: Match each subprogram to its description.
right: Performs actions with no returned value
Sends the result back to the caller
Requests the execution of a subprogram
questions.explanation: These are the key words of subprograms.

questions.question: Which is a **function**?
options: DisplayArea(radius), which only displays the area
questions.explanation: A function provides a result. The others only perform an action.

questions.question: Which is a **procedure**?
options: WelcomeMessage(name), which only displays Hello, name
questions.explanation: A procedure does not return a value.

questions.question: In GetCircumference with PI = 3.14, what is returned for radius = 5? (2 × PI × radius)
In DisplayArea with PI = 3.14, what area is displayed for radius = 5? (PI × radius × radius)
Complete the function that returns the sum of two numbers.
questions.code:
Function Sum(a, b) {{1}} Integer
Begin
    {{2}} a + b
End Function
questions.explanation: A function declares the type it returns with Returns and sends the value back with Return.

questions.question: Complete the call that stores the result in c.
questions.explanation: We call the function, keep its result in c, and display c.

questions.question: A procedure can only be written once and can never be called twice.
questions.explanation: A subprogram can be called as many times as needed. That is the point of reusing it.
